sources.title: Scottish Archaeological Research Framework, Highland Early Medieval: Introduction
sources.note: Paragraphs on earliest references, Fortriu, later ninth-century power shifts, Alba and undeciphered symbols. Frontiers and political control remain uncertain.

sources.title: Susan Kruse, Portmahomack: The Tarbat Discovery Programme
sources.note: Periods 1-3, especially the paragraphs beginning Around AD 700, Around AD 800 and Shortly after the raid. Monastery and attacker identifications are interpretations.

sources.title: Scottish Archaeological Research Framework, Farming, Fishing and Hunter Gathering
sources.note: Cultivated Food: Lairg and Portmahomack; Domesticated Animals: Portmahomack. Grain remains, kiln conversion and cattle use are site-specific evidence.

sources.title: AOC Archaeology, An Early Medieval Enclosure at Rhynie, Aberdeenshire
sources.note: 2017 excavation account: fifth- and sixth-century enclosure sequence, ditch deposits, imported amphorae and glass, axe pin and clay moulds. Imports do not identify the people transporting them.

sources.title: Historic Environment Scotland, Hilton of Cadboll Chapel
sources.note: Overview: cross-slab erected about 800, hunting scene with central woman, later reworking and distinction between the original and the replica.

sources.title: Bede, Ecclesiastical History of England, translated by A. M. Sellar
sources.note: Book II chapters 3 and 5 for Mellitus, Sabert and London; book V chapter 21 for Naiton, Ceolfrid, Easter and stone builders. Bede writes from a Christian ecclesiastical perspective.

sources.title: English Heritage, History of St Augustine's Abbey
sources.note: Augustine's Mission and Reforms, raids and relics: Bertha, arrival in 597, probable foundation in 598, precincts, school and later tenth-century reform. Later unsupported generalizations are not adopted.

sources.title: Rochester Cathedral, Textus Roffensis
sources.note: Description of the early-1120s compilation and its two constituent books, including earlier Kentish law codes. The surviving manuscript is not contemporary with the seventh-century laws.

sources.title: Christopher Monk, Aethelberht's Code, c. 600 CE
sources.note: Complete translation, folios 1r-3v: church property, free and enslaved people, compensation for injuries. Prescriptions are evidence of legal categories, not a record of every case or actual enforcement.

sources.title: University of Reading, Anglo-Saxon royal entertainment uncovered in Kent
sources.note: 22 November 2013 report: hollow bone gaming piece with lathe-turned caps and bronze rivet; late-sixth- and seventh-century royal setting, glass and animal bones. Precise rules of play are unknown.

sources.title: Gabor Thomas, Life before the Minster: the Social Dynamics of Monastic Foundation at Anglo-Saxon Lyminge, Kent
sources.note: Antiquaries Journal 93 (2013), pp. 133-138: fish signatures, changing livestock proportions, textile tools and limits of dietary interpretation. The zooarchaeological assessment is explicitly provisional.

sources.title: University of Reading, Viking brutality failed to wipe out community, dig finds
sources.note: 30 January 2023: radiocarbon-dated butchered bones, 804 asylum record, later coins and rebuilding, abandonment by the late ninth century and subsequent tenth-century settlement.

sources.title: Ann Williams, The Vikings in Essex, 871-917
sources.note: Essex Archaeology and History 27 (1996), pp. 92-101, especially p. 92 (PDF page 96): Mercian overlordship, West Saxon takeover around 825, subordinate kingdom until 860 and later administration. Sigered's expulsion is described as probable.

sources.title: Southend Museums, The Princely Burial
sources.note: Discovery and History and Dating: timber chamber, hanging bowl, gold crosses, radiocarbon and coin range 580-605. The page's claim that this whole range precedes 597 is mathematically incorrect and is not adopted.

sources.title: MOLA, Prittlewell princely burial secrets revealed in new research
sources.note: 9 May 2019: painted maple box and lyre sections; micro-excavation, wood identification, repairs and Raman analysis. Gemstone origin is probable; the burial does not securely name its occupant.

sources.title: Helena Hamerow, Excavations at Mucking, Volume 2: The Anglo-Saxon Settlement
sources.note: English Heritage Archaeological Report 21 (1993): introduction pp. 6-7; Grubenhauser discussion pp. 16-18, especially weaving, GH84 and GH105. Objects in backfill do not automatically demonstrate an activity in place.

sources.title: Historic England Research Record 1302386, Mucking
sources.note: Settlement summary: posthole buildings, sunken features and changing clusters. The fourth-century statement conflicts with the record's date fields and Hamerow's fifth-century dating; the primary report takes precedence.
